mechanism: Category-theory span with apex P=open long float and legs to domains A=ATR and B=MA: on each new bar log (float, ATR, MA); lagging correlations of A and B with P forecast negative drawdowns and drive a linear trailing stop δ_sl = (MA·m_ma+c_ma)+(ATR·m_atr+c_atr).
data_needed: Open long; per-bar float/profit; ATR and MA series; lagging correlation window; linear slope/intercept inputs for trailing class.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 (demo from 1 Mar; ~1y RSI-signal trailing tests)
why_new_for_mis: Frames ATR+MA as span legs whose lag-correlation to live P&L is an explicit volatility/drawdown sensor for stop placement, not just indicator levels.
quote: If we do lagging correlations between each of our two domain data sets A & B with the position profit, this can help set whether each of these domains could forecast negative drawdowns in a position.

mechanism: Reconstitute ATR/MA domains as composite spans: A=A'×C and B=C×B' with C=price, A'/B'=inverse periods; universal morphisms f'''/g''' between price and indicator periods refine stop morphisms while holding other coefficients fixed—fewer free inputs than full composite fit.
data_needed: ATR/MA period factors; price-sum / close-sum inputs; linear morphism coefficients; wizard trailing+signal EA.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a hierarchical feature graph: period↔price universal maps as first-class sensors for adaptive exits beyond raw ATR multiples.
quote: Firstly, in the domain A span, since domain A' and domain C, are terminal, a universal morphism is implied between A' and C.

mechanism: WeighTimeframes scores each candidate TF by 10000·|Δclose01|/(|Δclose01|+|Δclose12|) from last 3 bars, then OperateModulo maps integer weights into a circular monoid-group; same weighting pattern applied to lookback, applied-price, indicator, and trade-method decision monoids with inversion/identity axioms for selection.
data_needed: CopyRates for each ENUM_TIMEFRAMES candidate (3 bars); integer weights; modulo group size (odd); monoid binary op (furthest-from-identity).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY.i M1 chart host; multi-TF candidates; lookback/applied-price/indicator decision pools
why_new_for_mis: Turns relative consecutive-bar move balance into a normalized sensor that selects which TF/feature pool is currently informative—adaptive meta-sensing for MIS feature routers.

mechanism: Encode each bar as a directed graph path over vertices {O,H,L,C}; bullish bars often O-L-H-C vs default O-H-L-C. Lagging path types are tested as predictors of subsequent bar high/low range and used to adjust a custom Expert Trailing (paired with Awesome Oscillator signal, fixed-margin MM).
data_needed: Per-bar OHLC order/path class; subsequent range labels; wizard EA with TrailingCT_11.
why_new_for_mis: Treats intra-bar visit order as a discrete change/path sensor for near-term range—MIS can stream OHLC-path state without waiting for full candle patterns.
quote: Supposing we consider a single price bar that has the typical four prices of open, high, low and close. We could deem these a path because usually their order is not always O-H-L-C. In bullish bars, though not always, the order could be O-L-H-C.

mechanism: Trade pipeline vertices (timeframe→lookback→applied-price→indicator→trade-action) with fixed ends; iterate mid-step order as alternate graphs; hypothesize no ideal order and forecast next graph homomorphism from the last two to set trailing stops on predicted range change.
data_needed: Enumerated step-order graphs; homomorphism sequence; range-change target; trailing class.
why_new_for_mis: Elevates decision-pipeline topology itself into a sensor—MIS can track which feature-ordering graph is live and whether homomorphism forecasts signal regime shift in system structure.
quote: we will try to project the next graph homomorphism given, say, the most recent two.
